newsitem.title: USA: Parker & Parsley value of proved reserves up.
newsitem.headline: Parker & Parsley value of proved reserves up.

text.p: Parker & Parsley Petroleum Co said Wednesday that in 1996 it added 45 million barrels (MMBLS) of crude oil and 181 billion cubic feet (Bcf) of natural gas or 75 million barrel oil equivalents (MMBOE).

As of December 31, 1996, total proved oil and gas reserves were 164 MMBLS of crude oil and 829 BCF of natural gas. Combined, these reserves are equivalent to 302 MMBLS of crude oil or 1.8 trillion cubic feet of natural gas.

The company's reserve mix is balanced at 54 percent oil and 46 percent gas which has allowed the company to benefit significantly from the current strong oil and gas price environment. The SEC value of the total proved oil and gas reserves increased 64 percent to $2.3 billion from $1.4 billion in 1995.

The 75 MMBOE added represents a reserve replacement rate of 314 percent of 1996 production of 24 MMBOE. The increase in oil and gas reserves is directly attributable to the company's 1996 drilling program in which the company drilled in excess of 600 wells.

In 1996, the company spent $233 million in capital expenditures and achieved a finding and development cost of $3.10 per BOE. For the three year period (1994-1996), the company achieved an average finding and development cost of $3.99 per BOE and reserve replacement rate of 377 percent.

Despite the sale during 1996 of nonstrategic properties, which accounted for 46 MMBOE or 15 percent of the year end 1995 reserves, the company's year end 1996 total proved oil and gas reserves increased 2 percent to 302 MMBOE. Crude oil reserves increased to 164 MMBLS from 147 MMBLS at year end 1995.

Total proved gas reserves decreased to 829 Bcf from 897 Bcf at year end 1995. The year end 1996 total proved oil and gas reserves increased 20 percent after adjusting the 1995 year end reserves downward by 46 MMBOE for nonstrategic properties sold during 1996.
